```{r setup}
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(sf); library(ggplot2); library(glue)
  library(patchwork); library(knitr); library(scales); library(purrr)
})
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/helpers.R")

# The helpers read PAL at call time, so overriding it converts every figure in
# the deck to the dark palette without touching a plot definition.
PAL <- modifyList(PAL, list(
  ink = "#F4E7DF", ground = "#2B1512", ground_alt = "#3A1D18",
  rule = "#593029", muted = "#C3A79B", null = "#4A2A24", border = "#2B1512",
  accent = "#E2574C", accent_dk = "#F2A08F", accent_lt = "#9E4A40",
  cool = "#5FB3BC", cool_lt = "#2F6E75",
  seq = c("#2B1512", "#4F201B", "#7A2C25", "#A8392F", "#D2513F", "#EE8466", "#FBC9B4")))

P <- readRDS(file.path(DIR_DERIVED, "prepared.rds"))
L <- readRDS(file.path(DIR_DERIVED, "lmsa.rds"))
E <- readRDS(file.path(DIR_DERIVED, "ehsa.rds"))
D <- readRDS(file.path(DIR_DERIVED, "diffusion.rds"))

tsp <- P$tsp; ev <- P$ev
states <- tsp |> group_by(ST) |> summarise(.groups = "drop")
tsp_attr <- st_drop_geometry(tsp) |> select(TS_PCODE, TS, ST, pv)
with_geo <- function(df) tsp |> select(TS_PCODE, TS, ST) |> left_join(df, by = "TS_PCODE")
var_lab <- function(v) factor(VAR_LABELS[v], levels = VAR_LABELS)
ehsa_pv <- E$ehsa |> filter(var == "pv") |> left_join(tsp_attr, by = "TS_PCODE")
tb <- D$tab
on_none <- tb$p_active_next[tb$from == "Quiet" & tb$ctx == D$ctx_lab[1]]
on_most <- tb$p_active_next[tb$from == "Quiet" & tb$ctx == D$ctx_lab[3]]
or_most <- D$or_tab |> filter(term == "ctxMost neighbours active")
ph <- function(phase, ctx) D$phase_tab$p_active_next[D$phase_tab$from == "Quiet" &
                                                     D$phase_tab$phase == phase & D$phase_tab$ctx == ctx]
yr <- st_drop_geometry(ev) |> mutate(y = format(event_date, "%Y")) |>
  group_by(y) |> summarise(air = sum(sub_event_type == "Air/drone strike"))
mapt <- function(base = 13) list(coord_sf(expand = FALSE, datum = NA), theme_map(base_size = base))
kf <- function(...) {
  items <- list(...)
  cat('<div class="kf">')
  for (it in items) cat(sprintf('<div><div class="n">%s</div><div class="l">%s</div></div>', it[[1]], it[[2]]))
  cat('</div>')
}
```

## Contents {.smaller}

::: {.subhead}
One question in three parts: where violence clusters, how that is changing, and
whether it spreads from one township to the next.
:::

1. The question, the place and the data
2. Clearing the land mines
3. A war that changed its means
4. Where violence clusters
5. Every kind of violence, the same core
6. Which way the trends run
7. Emerging hot spots
8. Violence spreads to neighbours
9. Fronts, not sparks
10. What this means for peace-building, and what it cannot say

## 1. The question, the place and the data

```{r}
#| output: asis
kf(list(fmt_n(nrow(ev)), "political-violence events"),
   list(nrow(tsp), "townships, MIMU 9.4"),
   list(length(P$quarters), "quarters"),
   list("2021-25", "Jan 2021 to Sep 2025"))
```

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-map}
#| out-width: "46%"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 3.6
ggplot(tsp) + geom_sf(aes(fill = pv), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_count(v = tsp$pv) + mapt(11) + theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::
::: {.note}
**Where does armed conflict in Myanmar cluster, how is it changing, and does it
spread?** Since the coup of February 2021 the war has moved from the borderlands
into the Bamar heartland, and it has kept moving.

**Data.** ACLED events (battles, explosions and remote violence, violence against
civilians), joined by location to the 330 MIMU township polygons. Protests and
strategic developments are excluded: they are not armed conflict.

**Approach.** Local Moran's I and Gi* for where; a 19-quarter space-time cube with
Mann-Kendall and emerging hot spot analysis for how it changes; a spatial Markov
chain for whether it spreads.

*Darker townships on the map have more events; the dry zone and the Thai border
stand out.*
:::
:::

## 2. Clearing the land mines

::: {.split .even .roomy}
::: {.col}
[What I removed]{.colhead}

**`r P$qa$indian_ocean` events coded to the Indian Ocean.**

**`r P$qa$geo3_pv` events placed on a regional centroid** (geo_precision 3). Kept,
they would pile false violence onto whichever township holds the centroid.

**`r fmt_n(P$qa$admin3_na_pv)` events have no township name**, so I joined every
event by its coordinates, not its name. A name join would have lost all of them.
:::
::: {.note}
[What I kept but distrust]{.colhead}

**Fatalities.** The top 1% of events carry `r fmt_pct(P$qa$fat_share_top1pct)`
of reported deaths. Analysed, never used to build the cube.

**Zeros in Wa and Mongla.** `r P$qa$zero_tsp` townships record nothing in five
years; seven are in ceasefire enclaves that report almost nothing. They anchor a
cold spot that partly measures silence.

**Skew.** Counts run from 0 to `r fmt_n(max(tsp$pv))`. The statistics use
log(1 + count), checked against raw counts.
:::
:::

## 3. A war that changed its means

```{r sl-series}
#| fig-height: 4.1
#| fig-width: 11
mon <- P$qa$monthly |> mutate(type = var_lab(var))
type_cols <- c(PAL$accent, "#F2A08F", PAL$cool) |> setNames(VAR_LABELS[c("battles", "erv", "vac")])
ggplot(mon, aes(month, n, colour = type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(COUP_DATE, OP1027_DATE), colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "22") +
  annotate("text", x = c(COUP_DATE, OP1027_DATE) + 25, y = Inf, vjust = 1.4, hjust = 0,
           label = c("Coup", "Operation 1027"), size = 4, colour = PAL$muted) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = type_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Events per month") + theme_ex02(base_size = 15)
```

::: {.subhead}
Violence climbed through 2021 and peaked with Operation 1027 in November 2023.
**Explosions and remote violence overtook battles in 2023**, driven by the
military's air campaign: `r yr$air[yr$y == "2021"]` air or drone strikes in 2021,
`r fmt_n(yr$air[yr$y == "2024"])` in 2024. An air strike lands where the military
chooses, not where the fighting is.
:::

## 4. Where violence clusters

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-lisa}
#| fig-height: 4.9
#| fig-width: 6.2
lm <- with_geo(L$lisa |> filter(var == "pv")) |> mutate(cls = factor(cls, names(LISA_COLS())), panel = "Local Moran's I")
gm <- with_geo(L$gi |> filter(var == "pv")) |>
  mutate(cls = recode(cls, "Hot spot" = "High-High", "Cold spot" = "Low-Low"),
         cls = factor(cls, names(LISA_COLS())), panel = "Gi*")
ggplot(bind_rows(lm, gm) |> mutate(panel = factor(panel, c("Local Moran's I", "Gi*")))) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = cls), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LISA_COLS(), drop = TRUE, name = NULL,
                    labels = c("High-High / hot spot", "Low-High", "Low-Low / cold spot", "Not significant")) +
  mapt(12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") + guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```
:::
::: {.note}
All political violence, p < 0.05, 999 permutations.

**Global Moran's I is `r round(L$global$I[L$global$var == "pv"], 2)`.** A
township's violence is very well predicted by its neighbours'.

**One dominant core: the dry zone** of Sagaing, Magway and Mandalay, with a second
belt down the Thai border through Kayin, Mon and Tanintharyi.

**Cold spots:** the Ayeyarwady delta, Yangon and eastern Shan.

**No High-Low outliers at all.** Violence in Myanmar does not form islands; it
comes in neighbourhoods.

*82 to 96% of townships keep their class under raw counts or 6-nearest-neighbour
weights. About half survive a false discovery rate correction: the cluster cores.*
:::
:::

## 5. Every kind of violence, the same core

```{r sl-types}
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 11.5
lt <- with_geo(L$lisa |> filter(var != "pv")) |>
  mutate(var = var_lab(var), cls = factor(cls, names(LISA_COLS())))
ggplot(lt) + geom_sf(aes(fill = cls), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.1) +
  facet_wrap(~var, nrow = 1, labeller = label_wrap_gen(18)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LISA_COLS(), name = NULL) + mapt(12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

::: {.subhead}
Local Moran's I by type. **Battles** add the ethnic fronts in Chin, Kachin and
Kayah. **Violence against civilians** is the most concentrated: 88% of its
High-High townships are in the dry zone. Fatalities follow battles.
:::

## 6. Which way the trends run

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-mk}
#| out-width: "56%"
#| fig-height: 4.9
#| fig-width: 4
mkm <- with_geo(E$mk |> filter(var == "pv")) |> mutate(fill = if_else(sl < ALPHA, tau, NA_real_))
ggplot(mkm) + geom_sf(aes(fill = fill), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.12) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = PAL$cool, mid = PAL$ground_alt, high = PAL$accent, midpoint = 0,
                       na.value = PAL$null, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Kendall's tau") +
  mapt(11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(26, "pt"))
```
:::
::: {.note}
Mann-Kendall test on each township's 19-quarter Gi* series, p < 0.05.

```{r}
#| include: false
mk_pv <- E$mk |> filter(var == "pv") |> left_join(tsp_attr, by = "TS_PCODE")
yg <- mk_pv |> filter(ST == "Yangon")
```

**Cooling: Yangon.** `r sum(yg$trend == "Falling")` of its `r nrow(yg)` townships
have a falling Gi*. The urban resistance of 2021 is gone from the map.

**Warming: the middle belt.** Bago West, Mandalay, Magway, Bago East and
Tanintharyi, where the war arrived late as the dry-zone insurgency spread and new
fronts opened.

**Sagaing barely registers**, because it was hot from 2021 and stayed hot. A trend
test cannot see a level, which is the gap emerging hot spot analysis fills.
:::
:::

## 7. Emerging hot spots

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-ehsa}
#| out-width: "72%"
#| fig-height: 4.9
#| fig-width: 4.3
em <- with_geo(E$ehsa |> filter(var == "pv")) |> mutate(classification = factor(classification, EHSA_LEVELS))
present <- levels(droplevels(em$classification))
cols <- EHSA_COLS(); cols["no pattern detected"] <- PAL$null
ggplot(em) + geom_sf(aes(fill = classification), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.12) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols[present], breaks = present, labels = ehsa_label(present), name = NULL) +
  mapt(10) + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key.width = unit(10, "pt"))
```
:::
::: {.note}
```{r}
#| include: false
nm <- function(c) paste(ehsa_pv$TS[ehsa_pv$classification == c], collapse = ", ")
```
**Intensifying, the most urgent:** `r nm("intensifying hotspot")`. Hot in nearly
every quarter and still rising, five of six in the dry zone.

**Consecutive, a front that moved and held:** Kyaukkyi and Shwegyin through
Kyaikto and Bilin to Kawkareik and Myawaddy on the Thai border.

**Oscillating** hot spots fill Sagaing and Magway. Not unstable: they were cold in
the coup quarter, before the resistance existed, and have been hot since.

**Persistent cold spots** are the Shan hills, including Wa and Mongla.

*Fine classes are fragile: 62% of townships keep their label on a monthly cube,
78% keep hot/cold/neither. Every label was checked against an independent Gi\*
series, because sfdep 0.2.5 can attach labels to the wrong townships.*
:::
:::

## 8. Violence spreads to neighbours

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-markov}
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 6.2
q <- D$tab |> filter(from == "Quiet") |> mutate(ctx = factor(ctx, D$ctx_lab))
ggplot(q, aes(ctx, p_active_next)) +
  geom_col(fill = PAL$accent, width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_pct(p_active_next)), vjust = -0.5, size = 6, colour = PAL$ink) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No neighbour\nactive", "Some\nneighbours", "Most\nneighbours")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 0.45)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Quiet township active\nnext quarter") + theme_ex02(base_size = 15)
```
:::
::: {.note}
**Value-added: a spatial Markov chain.** Each township-quarter is active (3 or
more events) or quiet. Does a quiet township's chance of becoming active depend on
its neighbours?

**Yes, by a factor of four:** `r fmt_pct(on_none)` with no active neighbour,
`r fmt_pct(on_most)` with most neighbours active.

**It is not just "a violent region".** With fixed effects for state and quarter and
the township's own history, the odds ratio is `r round(or_most$OR, 1)` (bootstrap
`r round(or_most$lo, 1)` to `r round(or_most$hi, 1)`). Shuffling townships'
histories across the map never reproduces the gap (p `r fmt_p(D$p_perm, 499)`).
It holds at 1, 3 and 6 events.

*Out of sample it is a modest signal: AUC `r round(D$oos$auc[1], 2)` from own
history, `r round(D$oos$auc[2], 2)` with neighbours.*
:::
:::

## 9. Fronts, not sparks

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-watch}
#| out-width: "56%"
#| fig-height: 4.9
#| fig-width: 4
wm <- with_geo(D$watch |> select(TS_PCODE, share))
ggplot(wm) + geom_sf(aes(fill = share), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.12) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#2F4F55", PAL$cool, "#E9A07F", PAL$accent),
                       na.value = PAL$null, labels = label_percent(), name = "Neighbours active") +
  mapt(11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(26, "pt"))
```
:::
::: {.note}
**Since Operation 1027, isolated outbreaks have almost stopped.** A quiet township
with no active neighbour ignited
`r fmt_pct(ph("Before Operation 1027", D$ctx_lab[1]))` of the time before the
offensive and `r fmt_pct(ph("From Operation 1027", D$ctx_lab[1]))` after. Onset
next to active neighbours did not change
(`r fmt_pct(ph("Before Operation 1027", D$ctx_lab[3]))` and
`r fmt_pct(ph("From Operation 1027", D$ctx_lab[3]))`).

New violence now appears at the edge of existing violence: a war of consolidated
fronts rather than the scattered uprising of 2021.

**The map:** townships quiet in 2025 Q3, shaded by the share of neighbours active.
The warmest are where the evidence says to look next, most of them in Magway,
Sagaing, Kachin and Mandalay. *Not a validated forecast.*
:::
:::

## 10. What this means, and what it cannot say

::: {.split .even}
::: {.col}
[For peace-building]{.colhead}

**Prioritise the intensifying hot spots** (Madaya, Myingyan, Seikphyu, Yesagyo,
Ngazun, Dawei) for protection and humanitarian access: established violence that is
still rising.

**Watch the quiet edges, not the centres.** Early warning and preparedness belong
in quiet townships beside active ones.

**Treat the southeast as a moving front**, where cross-border routes from Thailand
matter most.

**Plan for air-strike exposure beyond battle lines.** Battle maps alone will not
locate it.
:::
::: {.note}
[Limitations]{.colhead}

**ACLED counts reports, not violence.** Hot spots partly reflect visibility; the Wa
and Mongla zeros are the clearest case. A cold spot is not proof of safety.

**Counts, not rates.** No reliable township population exists for 2021-2025.

**Scale and neighbours.** Townships run from under 1 km² to over 12,000 km², and
contiguity treats every border as equally permeable.

**EHSA depends on the window**, which starts in the coup quarter, and its fine classes
move with parameter choices.

**Diffusion is descriptive.** An advancing front and contagion look alike at
quarterly resolution.
:::
:::
